memoryText: In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. The week you have completed introduced the man at the center of the rest of the Bible, Abraham. Take time today to let the sweep of his calling settle. The promise made to him is the promise that reaches you.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Genesis 12:3 is the seed of the gospel in the Old Testament. Paul calls it the gospel preached to Abraham (Galatians 3:8). The promise made to one man is the promise that ultimately reaches every nation, every family, every reader.

Say the verse aloud, and notice what is and is not promised. It does not promise Abraham personal prosperity. It does not promise his descendants ease. It promises blessing, and blessing of a particular kind, blessing that flows outward. Abraham is blessed in order to be a blessing.

The same is true of you. If you are in Christ, you are a child of Abraham (Galatians 3:7). The blessing of Abraham, flowing through Christ, has reached you. And it has not reached you so that it stops with you. You have been blessed in order to be a blessing. Carry the verse this week with two questions: How has God blessed me through Abraham’s offspring, Jesus? And to whom is he sending that blessing through me?
weekInReview:
This week was the great narrowing. After Unit 2 ended with the scattering of Babel, God called one man, Abram, and through him began the redemption of all the nations he had just scattered. You read Abram’s call in Genesis 12 and watched him obey, even with his failures. You met Melchizedek, the priest-king who prefigures Christ. You read the formal cutting of the Abrahamic Covenant in Genesis 15, with God alone walking between the pieces. You sat with the doctrinal pause on Covenant Theology, the structure that runs through the entire Bible. You worshiped with Psalm 105:1-22, which sings the patriarchal promise. And you read the Hagar story and the renewal of the covenant in Genesis 17.

The week’s center of gravity is the covenant. God binds himself to one family so that, through that family, all families of the earth will be blessed.
reflectionQuestions: Where in your life have you been trying to fulfill God’s promises through your own scheming? Sarai’s proposal of Hagar was the practical, culturally accepted alternative to waiting. It produced bitterness, blame, and broken relationships. Where are you tempted to engineer what God has already promised to provide? What would it look like to wait instead?

What does it mean that you, a Gentile reader, are included in the promise of Genesis 12:3? In Galatians 3, Paul says that those who are of faith are children of Abraham, that the blessing promised to all nations has come to you through Christ. Sit with this. You are part of the answer to Abraham’s calling. How does that reshape your sense of identity, your sense of mission, your sense of belonging?

How did the doctrinal pause on Covenant Theology this week clarify your reading of the Bible? Covenant is the structure through which God relates to his people from Noah to Christ. What is one specific way this framework has begun to change how you understand the Bible as one unified story?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that you are a child of Abraham by faith, brought near by Christ.
Thank Christ for keeping the covenant that you could not.
Ask him to make you a blessing to someone this coming week.
